question: Which of the following dance forms is mentioned in the ancient text of Vyavaharmala?
solution:
The correct answer is__** Mohiniyattam.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kerala** is where the** Indian classical dance style** known as** mohiniyattam** was born and has since flourished.
 
• The word **Mohini** is the source of the term "Mohiniyattam dance."
 
• The term "mohini" refers to a **historical enchantress and Vishnu avatar **who, by harnessing her feminine powers, aids in the** triumph of good over evil.**
 
• Both the **1709 work Vyavaharamala** by **Mazhamagalam Narayanan Namputiri** and the subsequent poem** Ghoshayatra** by poet **Kunjan Nambiar** contain references to Mohiniyattam.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sattriya:**

 
 
• A notable form of** Indian classical dance** is sattriya.
 
• **Ankiya Nat, one-act dramas** that Sankardev originally produced, are performed as part of **Bhaona,** where this dance was first established. 
 
 
 
• Manipuri:
 
 
• One of the eight principal Indian traditional dance styles, the Manipuri Dance is a product of the state of Manipur.
 
• The spiritual themes of Madhura Raas of Radha-Krishna are infused into the dance style.
 
• Gentle gaze and calm, serene body movements define it.
 
 
 
• Odissi dance:
 
 
• The temples of Odisha are where the odissi dance had its start.
 
• Throughout its history, women predominately performed odissi.
 
• Through songs, it conveyed spiritual and religious beliefs, particularly those of Vaishnavism.
